page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge is a dedicated GPU-accelerated virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading, alongside 32 GB of system memory, which establishes a 4 GB per vCPU memory density. The instance incorporates an L3 cache of 40 MB and includes hardware acceleration via a single NVIDIA Pascal P4 GPU equipped with 8 GB of VRAM. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps and operates without bundled local instance storage, requiring remote storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the architectural age of the Broadwell-based host processor. The instance recorded a stress-ng single-core score of 953.38 and a multi-core score of 4755.08, placing host processing performance in the lower tiers of comparative benchmarks. PassMark CPU execution reached 6698.53, while PassMark memory scores registered at 1780.34. System memory throughput measures 37.18 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 25.34 GB/sec for writes. Application benchmarks demonstrate 5.48 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 6.06 GB/sec.

The ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge presents a hardware profile structured for GPU-centric tasks where host CPU computational density is secondary. Because CPU throughput and memory bandwidth benchmark in lower brackets, workloads heavily reliant on complex host-side operations or massive local I/O will face architectural bottlenecks. The presence of the dedicated NVIDIA P4 GPU makes the instance an economical platform for entry-level neural network inference, batch image classification, video transcoding, and legacy CUDA compute pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance configured with 8 vCPUs, 32 GB of RAM, and an NVIDIA Pascal P4 graphics processing unit with 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor with 4 physical cores and hyperthreading, the instance relies on KVM virtualization and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. It features no local storage, requiring reliance on external block volumes. Synthetic benchmarks place the host CPU and memory throughput in the lower percentiles, with a stress-ng multi-core result of 4755.08 and PassMark CPU score of 6698.53. As a result, CPU-intensive operations face architectural constraints relative to modern platforms. The platform functions as a cost-accessible accelerator option tailored for light machine learning inference, computer vision processing, and legacy video encoding workloads.
